briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. I will now begin the climate briefing for October 31, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Global Health Emergency and the Accelerating Climate Crisis
sections.content: Today's news clearly demonstrates that the climate crisis is evolving into a global health emergency. With 3 million deaths attributed to heatwaves, global health has entered an emergency phase [1], leading to strong calls for the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare climate change a public health emergency [29]. In the Asia-Pacific region, climate change is threatening malaria eradication efforts [23], and analysis indicating the world is rapidly approaching the 1.5°C global warming target since the Paris Agreement underscores the urgency of the current situation [25]. The widespread occurrence of large sinkholes across Turkey due to drought and climate change [18], along with a decrease in wine harvests in Greece [28], also warn of the extensive threats climate change poses to our lives and environment, with Bloomberg.com reporting that humanity has been placed on permanent alert due to climate change [20].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Carbon Neutrality Transition Efforts and Current Challenges
sections.content: Domestically, various regional efforts are underway to achieve carbon neutrality. Hwasun County is conducting a carbon neutrality campaign with the Rural Leaders Association [5], and the Chungnam Credit Guarantee Foundation has launched the province's first working-level council for public institution carbon neutrality [6, 12]. Asan City Council's Special Committee on Carbon Neutrality is continuously strengthening its policy response capabilities by promoting expert lectures, policy development, and capacity-building training for its members to find region-specific solutions [7, 8, 9, 10, 11]. There is also positive news regarding renewable energy. Paju City won an Energy Transition Award for providing renewable energy to businesses and electricity bill savings to citizens [15], and OCI Holdings' solar power business is performing well [17]. However, bottlenecks are occurring where electricity generated from renewable energy cannot be transmitted [13], and despite power generation companies issuing green bonds worth 5.7 trillion KRW, insufficient investment in new and renewable energy has been pointed out [16], indicating the need for in-depth discussions on the sincerity and efficiency of domestic energy transition.

sections.title: 🌍 International Community's Climate Policies and Perception Status
sections.content: The international community continues its policy discussions and preparations for responding to climate change. An International Legal Forum on Climate Change was held in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam [4], and the Center on Global Energy Policy (CGEP) announced new personnel to strengthen climate change expertise [21]. Furthermore, ahead of the COP31 Climate Summit, the South African Minerals Council released its 2026 climate change position [31], and Brazilian President Lula is scheduled to attend the UN COP31 Climate Summit in Türkiye [35]. Meanwhile, challenges still exist in the perception and approach to climate change. In New Zealand, a businessman sparked controversy by offering the Green Party 150 million KRW if they could prove the existence of climate change [2], and in Florida, there have been calls to remove climate change-related content from textbooks [27, 30]. This demonstrates that social and political debates, beyond scientific consensus, still persist regarding climate change.

sections.title: ⚠️ Complex Impacts of Climate Change and the Importance of Adaptation
sections.content: Climate change is affecting our society and environment in unexpected and complex ways, making adaptation efforts increasingly crucial. In some cities, the possibility that climate change could trigger gun violence has been raised [26], and the Morton Arboretum is tracking the impact of climate change on fall foliage color changes, observing long-term ecosystem shifts [19, 22]. To cope with these changes, Himalayan communities are relying on centuries-old traditional water solutions [24]. Interestingly, the forecast that Sweden's solar power generation will increase by 5% due to reduced spring snowfall caused by climate change [3] suggests that unexpected 'benefits' might arise in some areas, but this cannot be a fundamental solution to climate change. The UK government recommends preparing for unexpected emergencies such as floods and power outages, and survival experts are providing preparation methods, emphasizing the urgent need for society-wide adaptation efforts against disasters that could be exacerbated by climate change [34].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has clearly highlighted the severity of the climate crisis, alongside the diverse domestic and international efforts and challenges in addressing it. We require a deeper understanding of the complex impacts of climate change, coupled with a resolute commitment to more swift and genuine responses. This concludes today's climate briefing.
